cells.tense: You are at the pen now, pausing in the middle of a session to ask again.
cells.act: cut through the inertia with one decisive act
cells.ask: When the same question comes around a fourth time, take the next step then, with the question still open.
cells.core:
You go into a session without knowing what will come out, and something sharper does come out. That is the current running through the repetitions: you turn a thing over, the hands find a piece of it, and the piece is better than the plan was. The practice is small and kept by hand, and it is teaching you on the days you show up tired.

The pull is to keep asking past the point of moving. The understanding is good, and it isn't the session. When the same question comes around a fourth time, take the next step then, right there, with the question still open. Tomorrow the question will be waiting, and there will be a piece of work beside it that didn't exist today.
cells.sheetLine: The question stays open. The next step is the one you take.
cells.verb: Turning a thing over with fresh questions until it gives up something.
cells.place: At a small repeated practice, kept by hand.

cells.tense: You are braced at a future that will not write itself, reaching past the hands.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Try a piece of the practice with no plan for where it leads, because beginning is what you feel like doing.
cells.core:
A finished version of the understanding is sitting in your head, bright and whole, and the sessions read like a slow march toward something you've already seen. Real certainty, not yet in the hands. The repetitions feel like catching up, so they get shortened while the ideas for them get longer.

Give that bright version somewhere to land. Try a piece of the practice with no destination — a page, a technique, a test whose point you don't yet know — and keep going until the work itself tells you what it is. Beginning is allowed to be the reason. The certainty isn't wrong. It just hasn't been through the hands that would make it useful.
cells.sheetLine: The certainty is finished in your head and not in your hands.
cells.verb: Turning a thing over with fresh questions until it gives up something.
cells.place: At a small repeated practice, kept by hand.

cells.tense: You are standing at a shut door, the practice behind you, the pen down.
cells.act: explore the feeling with fresh sensitivity
cells.ask: Sit with the practice as it is today and stay with whatever it stirs in you, without making anything come.
cells.core:
The sessions are still on the record and none of them are pulling. You look at what you were working on and it comes back the way familiar things do — known, flat, used up. Nothing in you steps toward it with a question anymore, and the understanding you once wanted isn't in view from where you stand.

Don't try to want it back by effort. Sit with the practice as it is today and look at where it actually is, not where it was. Stay a while with whatever surfaces in you while you sit there. If nothing comes, that is the answer for now and it doesn't need fixing from you. Sitting with a quiet thing without demanding it speak is its own kind of practice.
cells.sheetLine: You know the practice by heart and none of it is calling.

cells.tense: You have your hand on the pen without noticing that you are already writing.
cells.act: weigh what it costs them against what it gives
cells.ask: Where the practice touches someone else, make one fair call about the trade — what it takes from them, what it leaves — and stand by it.
cells.core:
You walk into a session, ask your question, and the answer shows up in your hands. It works, and the account you give is that you are just keeping busy. The practice is doing more than that, and your version of it is smaller than the practice is.

No bigger claims are needed. Somewhere in the practice there is a piece that costs someone else something — a stretch of time, a patience, an evening. Make one fair call about that piece and stand by the call without defending it. Honest accounting is what lets the practice speak as itself instead of through a story about keeping busy.
cells.sheetLine: The practice is doing the work. Your story calls it keeping busy.

attempts.check: The draft assumes the person has a practice at all; if they don't, the seat reads as a slight. The reader could reasonably say that what I call a reach forward is just enthusiasm — a good mood, not a capacity overshooting. The asks survive being wrong because each teaches something even from an empty practice: noticing what pulled, listening before choosing, keeping the smallest thing for a week, weighing the cost once. The sentence that serves me more than them is any soft general about 'the stuff you really want' — cut, replace with the explicit act.

attempts.check: The record supports a practice and a fresh-curiosity signature; it does not establish that the person has ever formally practised anything, so the seat is rendered as something small and repeated rather than as a named discipline. The reader could object that Too Much looks like ordinary eagerness and Too Little like ordinary tiredness — the difference I am claiming is where the person is standing relative to the work (in front of it, behind it), not what they feel, and I have kept the asks usable even if that read is wrong: each one is a plain act that works on an empty practice too. The sentence that serves me more than them is any soft line about 'the stuff you really want' — cut, replaced with the explicit act. Status 4's fair-call ask assumes the practice touches other people; where it doesn't, 'what it costs you against what it gives you' is the same act turned on one person.
